shapes.note: directory-walk burst: a cold burst longer than the cache, then the hot set (the scan-pollution case)

arms.note: S3-FIFO admission: a first touch enters a small probationary queue, only a re-referenced body is promoted to main; a one-pass scan is evicted without displacing the hot set
recency-only LRU: a scan burst longer than the cache evicts the whole hot set
the legacy unbounded resident map (nothing evicted); 100% residency but unbounded growth — the pre-admission baseline

shapes.note: reference shape: one cold inode then the whole hot set; the hot set stays within the cache window, so recency alone protects it

arms.note: S3-FIFO admission: a first touch enters a small probationary queue, only a re-referenced body is promoted to main; a one-pass scan is evicted without displacing the hot set
recency-only LRU: a scan burst longer than the cache evicts the whole hot set
the legacy unbounded resident map (nothing evicted); 100% residency but unbounded growth — the pre-admission baseline

note: Single-run, single-host court driving the LIVE manifested read path (namespace.Read -> manifest.Cache.ManifestedRead) over one identical scan-heavy trace; only the resident-body admission policy differs. This is a HIT-RATE measurement of the manifested-body cache (hits = served from an already-open certified body; misses = re-loaded and re-certified from the store), not a latency claim; p50_ns is reported but host- and timing-dependent. Admission never changes the bytes returned (see TestManifestAdmissionPreservesBytes). The burst shape shows the win: S3-FIFO, bounded, retains the hot set under a cold burst that flushes LRU; the unbounded map retains it too but without a bound. The interleaved shape shows the honest counter-case: when the hot set is re-referenced within the cache window, recency alone protects it and admission buys nothing over LRU.
